hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? which do you feel more often: that you’re too much, or not enough?
options: then this rabbi has something for your pocket. listen.
then he has something for that too. listen.

steps.line: In the Torah, God forms the first human from the dust of the ground. The ground is adamah. The human made from it is adam: the earthling.
Then God breathes into his nostrils the breath of life, “and man became a living soul.” Earth and breath, in one person.

steps.q: The breath God breathes in is neshamah in Hebrew. What does neshamah mean in Hebrew today?
steps.why: Soul. In Israel you’ll also hear “neshama” as a pet name, like “sweetheart.” The word that also means wind is a different one, ruach.

steps.line: In Poland, about two hundred years ago, a Hasidic teacher, Rabbi Simcha Bunim, told his students: everyone should have two pockets.
steps.label: a Hasidic story

steps.line: One slip says, “For my sake the world was created,” a saying of the rabbis. The other has Abraham’s words: “I am but dust and ashes.”
steps.label: a Hasidic story

steps.q: When should you reach for “For my sake the world was created”?
steps.why: When you feel low. And when you feel too proud, reach for the dust.

steps.line: When you feel too proud, reach for the dust. When you feel worthless, reach for the other pocket. The trick, he said, is knowing which one.

steps.q: You hurt a friend by mistake, and now you can’t stop calling yourself a terrible person. Which pocket?
o: “For my sake the world was created”
Neither: just apologize and move on
steps.why: Beating yourself up can feel humble, but it’s the worthless feeling. Reach for the world created for you: someone that precious can go and make it right.

steps.q: Abraham called himself “dust and ashes” at a bold moment. What was he doing?
o: Arguing with God to spare Sodom
steps.why: He was bargaining with God over Sodom: fifty good people, then forty-five, down to ten. He says “dust and ashes” and keeps arguing anyway: humble, and bold.

steps.line: Today, some people really do carry two slips of paper, one in each pocket. Earth and breath, both true of you, all the time.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. the word for formed is the word for a potter’s work. and god breathes into the human face to face. the breath of life came from very close.
the rabbis said the dust for the first human was gathered from all over the earth, so anywhere on earth could be home. you’re made of the ground, and of god’s breath.

steps.q: The Mishnah says “for my sake the world was created” right after asking why God began with one human. The reason?
o: Each single person is a whole world
Humans were meant to rule the animals
God wanted to start with something small
steps.why: Mishnah Sanhedrin: one human first, to teach that saving one life is like saving a whole world, and so no one can say “my ancestor was greater than yours.”

today.say: today, write the two lines on two small slips of paper, one for each pocket. when the day lifts you too high or pushes you too low, reach in. which line you need is up to you.
options: two pockets. you’ll know which one.
I’ll keep them in my phone
that works too. same two lines.

tomorrow.title: The man who slept seventy years.
tomorrow.line: a man watches a stranger plant a tree he’ll never eat from. then he lies down for a nap, and wakes up seventy years later.
